record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant C such that every convex body K in R^n admits an ellipsoid E with the following approximate sandwiching property: at least half the volume of E lies inside K, and at least half the volume of K lies inside the dilated ellipsoid C log n · E?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5. There exists a constant C such that for any convex body K in R^n, there exists an ellipsoid E that satisfies approximate sandwiching: vol(E ∩ K) ≥ 1/2 vol(E); vol(K ∩ C log nE) ≥ 1/2 vol(K).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$. A convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact convex set with non-empty interior, and an ellipsoid is the image of a Euclidean ball under an invertible affine map. For an ellipsoid $E$ centered at a point $x_0$ and a real number $t > 0$, write $tE := \{x_0 + t(y - x_0) : y \in E\}$ for the dilation of $E$ by factor $t$ about its center. Let $\mathrm{vol}(\cdot)$ denote $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure.

Decide whether the following statement holds: there exists an absolute constant $C > 0$ (independent of $n$ and of $K$) such that for every $n \geq 2$ and every convex body $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ there exists an ellipsoid $E \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ satisfying
$$\mathrm{vol}(E \cap K) \geq \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{vol}(E) \qquad\text{and}\qquad \mathrm{vol}(K \cap (C\log n)\,E) \geq \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{vol}(K).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture concerns an approximate ellipsoidal sandwiching with a $\log n$ factor, closely related to Milman's M-ellipsoid theory and to questions on covering numbers of convex bodies. Standard M-ellipsoid results give covering bounds and "half-volume" sandwiching with worse (polynomial-in-$n$) factors, while a $\log n$ sandwich would be a strong improvement. Web searches did not reveal a published proof or refutation of the precise statement, so the status is taken to be unknown / likely still open.

status_evidence.title: Near-optimal deterministic algorithms for volume computation via M-ellipsoids
status_evidence.snippet: An M-ellipsoid is intuitively the largest ellipsoid with roughly half its volume inside K; deterministic algorithms achieve covering bounds matching known lower bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Existing M-ellipsoid theory provides half-volume sandwiching but with polynomial (not logarithmic) covering/dilation factors.

status_evidence.title: The Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits Conjecture (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of isoperimetric and ellipsoidal questions in algorithmic convex geometry, with related open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys of related open problems do not record a resolution of the $C\log n$ approximate sandwiching conjecture.
